text:
Reid Schaefer was the 32nd pick in 2022 by his hometown Oilers, then went to Nashville the next season in the Mattias Ekholm trade. At 23 and 6-foot-5, he is a physical bottom-six winger trying to turn a depth role into a regular one.

Through 12 games he has one goal and two points at about 10.7 minutes a night, with 25 hits. His goal matches his chances almost exactly. His ice time is up about a minute over his last ten, and Nashville has been winning, though not because of what happens with him on the ice: the Predators control 43.6% of expected goals at five on five with him, a little worse than without him.

History gives the context. Of the 103 forwards picked 27 to 37 overall since 2005 who have had four-plus seasons, 40 reached 200 NHL games, and in their first season of 20-plus games they scored a median 0.33 points a game. Schaefer is at 0.17. His top shot speed ranks in the top quarter of the league, so watch whether he starts using it more often.
headline: Schaefer is still searching for his NHL role
